title: Connect governed clarification to the live Coding Agent Adapter

requirement.summary: Extend the vendor-neutral foreground Coding Agent stream so a normalized alignment observation automatically starts or resumes governed clarification, a strict human clarification update automatically returns the next question or final bounded choice, and the final human result returns only the resolved structured alignment state.

objective.rationale: The clarification state machine is useful only when a Coding Agent host can invoke it proactively in the ordinary foreground connection. Requiring users to author contracts or call a separate manual command would preserve the protocol but miss the product need for active, low-mechanical-input guidance.

goal: Add a strict alignment stream response and an in-memory foreground alignment session, dispatch alignment-context, clarification-update, and final human-decision-result records through agentgov dev --stream, automatically return exactly one next clarification prompt or one stable final decision prompt, and preserve existing lifecycle-stream compatibility and all denied authority.
non_goals: Do not send raw prompts, answers, transcripts, assistant responses, source content, credentials, model identifiers, or absolute host paths into AgentGov Core.
Do not claim Core semantically detects business or architecture drift from raw chat; the host Coding Agent Adapter must submit the strict normalized alignment context.
Do not persist dialogue across foreground process restarts, upload it, add a daemon, or add a second vendor-specific Adapter.
Do not let a Coding Agent submit a human clarification update or final direction selection.
Do not allow stale, duplicate, cross-dialogue, cross-prompt, cross-adapter, or out-of-order stream records to advance state.
Do not automatically edit requirements or ADRs, admit or replace a task, start a session, modify code or scope, execute commands, or authorize Git, deployment, publication, or release.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: A strict vendor-neutral alignment-stream response binds sequence, exact input identity, current dialogue revision, optional one-question clarification prompt, optional final human-decision prompt, status, and fully denied project authority.

The disclosed agentgov dev --stream process accepts strict agentgov.alignment-context 1.0 records alongside existing lifecycle events and immediately returns either the next one-question prompt or a final decision prompt without running a foreground development cycle.

The same stream accepts only a strict human-originated agentgov.clarification-update 1.0 bound to the active dialogue and exact last prompt, applies it in memory, and automatically returns the next question or stable final decision.

The same stream accepts only a strict agentgov.human-decision-result 1.0 bound to the active alignment decision prompt and returns resolved, stopped, or continued structured dialogue state without project mutation.

Duplicate contexts, missing active state, stale revisions, wrong prompts, cross-dialogue updates, Adapter drift, agent-authored human records, and unsupported contracts fail on the exact stream line before state advances.
The alignment session is memory-only for the disclosed foreground process; restart recovery and cross-process persistence are explicitly not claimed.

Existing coding-agent lifecycle JSONL events, response schema 1.2, cards, host interactions, human decisions, Codex Hooks, routing, session, scope, completion, packaging, and CLI behavior remain compatible.
Focused/full tests, all schema parsing, current-task, scope, repository, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_alignment_transport tests.test_clarification_dialogue tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_human_decision tests.test_codex_hooks tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A host Adapter could bias or fabricate the normalized center, drift, questions, answer summary, or recommendation while Core correctly validates only structure and identity.
Mixing alignment and lifecycle records in one stream could weaken existing strict parsing, event ordering, or adapter identity guarantees.
Returning a final choice too early could make unresolved ambiguity look governed.
Treating the in-memory dialogue as durable could lose context or misrepresent restart recovery.

stop_conditions: Stop if live integration requires Core to retain or interpret raw chat, transcript, source, credential, model, or absolute host-path content.
Stop if a Coding Agent can impersonate the human clarification or final decision actor.
Stop if an invalid alignment record can partially advance the in-memory session or invoke a lifecycle coordinator action.
Stop if alignment response display or resolution can mutate project, task, architecture, session, scope, code, Git, deployment, publication, or release state.
Stop if existing strict lifecycle stream events or response behavior becomes ambiguous or incompatible.
Stop before any Git write, Hook installation, release, consumer mutation, deployment, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the delivered live alignment transport and explicitly approved the next end-to-end natural-language Adapter rehearsal on 2026-08-06. This task is paused for routing hygiene only; the change does not claim acceptance, merge, publication, or release.
